# AGENTS.md - opencode-mobile

## Scope

Native Android and iOS client for an OpenCode V2 server (`opencode serve`, default port 4096).
The app pairs with a server, lists sessions, streams conversations live, sends prompts,
switches agent/model and answers permission requests. Code is shared with Kotlin
Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform; the Gradle build lives in `android/`.

Read the nearest nested `AGENTS.md` before changing a subsystem. Nested instructions take
precedence over this file.

## API Contract

The OpenCode server is the contract source. Never hand-write DTOs for server payloads.

```bash
cd tools/api-gen
bun run generate  # regenerate android/core/api from api/openapi.json
bun run refresh   # download openapi.json from the local service, pin its version, regenerate
bun run check     # fail when committed generated code is stale
```

Pipeline: `api/openapi.json` + event schemas from npm `@opencode/schema` (same version as
the server, pinned in `tools/api-gen/package.json`) -> `tools/api-gen` preprocessing ->
openapi-generator 7.22 (`kotlin`, `kotlinx_serialization`; models from `jvm-retrofit2`, APIs
from the Ktor-based `multiplatform` library) -> `android/core/api/src/commonMain`.

- Preprocessing only works around generator limitations (union discriminators, open structs,
  mixed primitive unions, deepObject params, unused API areas). Keep each step minimal and
  documented in `tools/api-gen/src/prepare-spec.ts`.
- To use a new API area, add its tag to `KEEP_TAGS` and regenerate.
- Generated code is committed so Gradle builds need neither Bun nor Nix.
- The event union is `io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.api.models.OpenCodeEvent`; REST unions such as
  `SessionMessageInfo` are sealed interfaces of `*Value`/`*Wrapper` wrappers.

## Server Access

- Authentication is HTTP Basic with username `opencode`. The password is the server password
  or a token obtained by pairing: `POST /api/pair` (authenticated) returns a short-lived code;
  `GET /auth/connect/{code}` with `Accept: application/json` returns `{ "token" }`.
- `opencode pair` prints pairing links and a QR for the phone; `--url` sets the address
  the phone should use (`opencode pair --url http://localhost:4096` for the emulator).
- On the emulator, `adb reverse tcp:4096 tcp:4096` maps the host server to `http://localhost:4096`.
  The iOS simulator shares the Mac's network: use the address of the OpenCode host.
- Phones reach the server over the LAN or a VPN. Never publish port 4096 to the internet:
  traffic is plain HTTP with Basic auth.
- Never print, log, commit or screenshot passwords, tokens or pairing codes. Scripts read
  credentials from environment variables (for example `OPENCODE_LIVE_PASSWORD`) and never
  echo them.
- Machine-specific notes (network, devices, credentials locations) stay outside the
  repository.

## Workflows

- Use `kmp-master` as the entry skill for Android and iOS work and `product-ux-orchestrator` for
  user-flow planning or audits.
- Commits and pull request titles follow Conventional Commits:
  `type(scope): Description`, see `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- Prompts sent during verification go only to a disposable session in a scratch directory,
  with a cheap model; never prompt in real sessions.
- After UI or behavior changes, install the debug build on the emulator and inspect the
  changed screen before finishing (see `android/AGENTS.md`); for iOS-specific code also run
  the app on the iOS simulator (macOS with Xcode).
- Before declaring Android work complete, run from `android/`
  `./gradlew spotlessCheck testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug`, and `bun run check` in

# Maestro E2E Tests

Black-box Android UI tests run with Maestro, used for testing only. Keep changes here
limited to flows, helpers and artifacts; app-side `testTag` changes belong under
`android/`. Load the `maestro` skill before editing.

## Running

```bash
# Debug build installed on an emulator with adb reverse tcp:4096 tcp:4096.
maestro --device <serial> test .maestro/smoke/launch.yaml .maestro/sessions/open-session.yaml

# Connect flow: pass a fresh single-use pairing code, never commit it.
OC_PAIR_CODE="$(opencode api post /api/pair --data '{}' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["code"])')"
maestro --device <serial> test -e OC_PAIR_CODE="$OC_PAIR_CODE" .maestro/connect/pair-manual.yaml
```

Output goes to the gitignored `.maestro/output/`. Command reports there contain typed
values, including pairing codes: delete them after debugging.

If Maestro reports "Android driver did not start up in time", another UiAutomator client
(usually Mobile MCP's `com.mobilenext.mobilecli.DeviceServer`) holds the device. Stop it
with `adb shell pkill -f mobilecli` and retry; Mobile MCP restarts it on demand.

## Flows

| Flow | Journey |
|---|---|
| `smoke/launch.yaml` | App starts on Connect or Sessions |
| `connect/pair-manual.yaml` | Clears data, pairs with URL + code, lands on Sessions |
| `sessions/open-session.yaml` | Searches sessions, opens one, returns |

## Rules

- `appId: io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.debug`.
- Interact only through `id:` selectors (Compose `testTag` exposed as resource IDs).
  Use text only to assert visible content.
- One flow per user journey; use `extendedWaitUntil` instead of sleeps.
- Never type or screenshot passwords; pairing codes come only from `-e` parameters.
- Do not send prompts in real sessions. Prompting flows create a session in a disposable
  scratch directory and use a cheap model.

# Android and iOS App Guidance

## Scope

`android/` is the Gradle build of the Android and iOS apps: Gradle 9.8.1, AGP 9.4.1, Kotlin
2.4.21 Multiplatform, Java 11, compile SDK 37, target SDK 36, min SDK 26, iOS 15+ (`iosArm64`,
`iosSimulatorArm64`). Every module except `:app` and `:core:testing` is a Kotlin Multiplatform
library (`com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library`); the UI uses Compose Multiplatform and
Material 3 themed with OpenCode V2 tokens; state uses MVI; Koin provides dependency
injection; the OpenCode HTTP client is generated (Ktor + kotlinx.serialization).

Use `kmp-master` as the entry skill. It routes to the smallest relevant specialist
skill set. Read the files you are changing and follow a nearby feature before introducing
a new pattern.

## Instruction Precedence

1. Explicit task requirements and behavior confirmed in the running app.
2. This `AGENTS.md` and the repository root `AGENTS.md`.
3. Project skills under `.opencode/skills/`.
4. Official vendor guidance compatible with the pinned versions.
5. External community guidance as advisory material only.

External guidance must never implicitly change the architecture, upgrade a major
dependency, introduce a new framework, bypass the design system, or bypass the
repository boundaries.

## Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `:app` | Android only: `OpenCodeApplication` (starts Koin), `MainActivity`, `appModule`, optional session notifications (`notifications/`: `SessionMonitor`, foreground service, permission reply receiver), home screen widget (`widget/`, Glance), share menu entry (`share/`: `ShareActivity` copies shared text and images into `ShareRepository`) |
| `:shared` | Shared by both apps: `OpenCodeApp` shell, root navigation (`AppNavHost`), `sharedModule` (ViewModels), widget model and loader (`widget/`); iOS entry point `MainViewController()`, `opencodemobile://` links and the widget snapshot for WidgetKit, in the `Shared` framework |
| `:feature:connect` | QR scan, paste link, manual URL + password/code, saved servers |
| `:feature:sessions` | Session list, search, project filter, create/rename/delete |

## Multiplatform Layout

- Sources live in `src/commonMain/kotlin`; platform code in `src/androidMain/kotlin` and
  `src/iosMain/kotlin` (interfaces bound in Koin, or `expect`/`actual` for small helpers;
  see the `kmp-platform-boundaries` skill). Pure-logic tests go in `src/commonTest/kotlin`
  with `kotlin.test` and run on the JVM and the iOS simulator; tests needing JVM tooling
  (MockWebServer, Robolectric, Room) live in `src/androidHostTest/kotlin`. Both run with
  `testAndroidHostTest`, also reachable as `testDebugUnitTest`.
- Keep `java.*`, `android.*`, OkHttp and Activity APIs out of `commonMain`. Use
  kotlinx-datetime, `kotlin.time.Clock`, `kotlin.uuid.Uuid`, atomicfu locks and Compose
  Multiplatform APIs instead.
- Android-only features stay in `androidMain` or `:app`; on iOS they are hidden
  (`notificationsSupported`) rather than faked. The home screen widget exists on both: Glance
  in `:app`, a WidgetKit extension in `iosApp/SessionsWidget` fed by the app (see the
  `kmp-ios` skill).

## Compose And MVI

- Each screen has `Event`, immutable `State` and one-shot `Effect` types; the ViewModel
  extends `BaseViewModel<State, Event, Effect>` and exposes one `onEvent`.
- `XxxRoute` resolves the ViewModel with `koinViewModel()`, collects state with
  `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` and effects with `CollectEffect`; `XxxScreen(state,
  onEvent)` is stateless and previewable.
- Use `Oc*` components and `OcTheme`/`MaterialTheme` tokens; no hard-coded colors in
  features. Tokens and components are documented in `docs/design-system.md`.
- Every interactive control has a stable `testTag`; the root enables
  `testTagsAsResourceId` for Maestro and UI Automator.
- Use stable keys in lazy lists; keep existing content during refresh.
- A nested `Scaffold` sets `contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets(0)` when a parent already
  handles system insets. Keep IME padding at the lowest container that must move.
- Strings live in Compose Multiplatform resources (`src/commonMain/composeResources/values*`,
  accessed through each module's generated `Res`) with English defaults and translations for
  Italian, Spanish, French, German, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese,
  Japanese, Korean and Arabic. Placeholders are positional only (`%1$s`, `%2$d`); write `'`,
  `"` and `%` unescaped. `:app` keeps Android resources for notifications. From the
  repository root, `bun test tools/locales.test.ts` checks translation coverage.

## Data And API

- The server contract is generated; never hand-write DTOs. See the root `AGENTS.md`.
- Features use repository interfaces from `core:domain`; failures are `OpenCodeError`.
- Live updates come from `EventRepository.events`; the chat applies them with
  `TranscriptReducer` and reloads from the server after reconnects and step ends.
- Transcripts are cached in Room (`core/data/cache`, KSP) and synced incrementally; see the
  `android-data-boundaries` skill before changing message loading.
- Never log or display passwords, pairing tokens/codes, Authorization headers, prompts or
  tool output in logs.

## Build And Verification

From `android/`:

```bash
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest
./gradlew :core:network:testDebugUnitTest
ANDROID_SERIAL=<serial> ./gradlew :app:installDebug
./gradlew spotlessApply   # ktlint formatting, rules in .editorconfig; core/api is excluded
ANDROID_SERIAL=<serial> ./gradlew :benchmark:connectedBenchmarkAndroidTest   # performance, see below
```

Performance is measured by the `:benchmark` Macrobenchmark module against the app's
`benchmark` build type (release code, offline demo data): idle frames and CPU, cold start
and list scrolling. It is not part of the checks before finishing; run it for the before
and after of a performance change (see the `android-benchmarks` skill). CI compiles the
benchmark sources (`:benchmark:compileBenchmarkKotlin`) and does not run them.

Before finishing: `./gradlew spotlessCheck testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug`
and `./gradlew compileKotlinIosArm64 compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64 compileTestKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
(what CI runs; iOS klibs compile on Linux too, and the test compile rejects test names Kotlin/Native
does not accept, such as names with commas), plus `bun run check` in `../tools/api-gen` when the API changed.

### iOS

Linking the `Shared` framework and building `../iosApp` need macOS with Xcode. From
`../iosApp`:

```bash
xcodebuild -project iosApp.xcodeproj -target iosApp -configuration Debug -sdk iphonesimulator \
  -arch arm64 CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=YES CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO build
xcrun simctl install booted build/Debug-iphonesimulator/OpenCodeMobile.app
xcrun simctl launch booted io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile
```

Ad-hoc signing embeds the entitlements the app needs at runtime: a build with
`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` (enough for CI, which only compiles) cannot store the server
password in the Keychain and fails to connect with error -34018.

The Xcode build phase runs `./gradlew :shared:embedAndSignAppleFrameworkForXcode` (needs
`JAVA_HOME`). Set `TEAM_ID` in `../iosApp/Configuration/Config.xcconfig` to sign for a device.

After every UI or behavior change, install the debug build (`io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.debug`)
on a running emulator and inspect the changed screen and Logcat. `adb reverse tcp:4096
tcp:4096` lets the app reach the host OpenCode server at `http://localhost:4096` (it is also
at `http://10.0.2.2:4096`). Bring the existing task back without force-stopping:

```bash
adb -s <serial> shell am start -n io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.debug/io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.MainActivity
adb -s <serial> logcat -d -v threadtime AndroidRuntime:E '*:S'
```

Do not hard-code an emulator serial; use the one reported by `adb devices` or the script.

---

# Android Server Connection And Credentials

The app has no user accounts. A "session" with a server is a saved
`ServerProfile`: base URL + Basic auth secret, owned by `ServerRepository`.

## Protocol

- Every request uses HTTP Basic `opencode:<secret>`.
- The secret is either the server password (`CredentialKind.Password`) or a
  pairing token (`CredentialKind.PairingToken`).
- Pairing: desktop runs `POST /api/pair` (authenticated) and shows
  `http(s)://host:port/auth/connect/<code>` as a QR (`opencode pair`).
  The app redeems it with an unauthenticated `GET /auth/connect/<code>` and
  `Accept: application/json`, receiving `{ "token" }`. Codes are single-use and
  expire after about five minutes.
- `ConnectLinkParser` (core:network) is the only parser for scanned, pasted or
  typed input. Bare hosts default to port 4096.

## Ownership

- `ServerRepository` owns saved profiles, the active server and validation
  (`probe`, `pair`, `addWithPassword`). Nothing else persists secrets.
- Secrets live in encrypted storage in `core:data`; UI state only holds what the
  user is typing until submit.
- The network client for the active server is rebuilt when the active profile
  changes; event streams restart on that change.

## Rules

- Validate before saving: a profile is persisted only after a successful
  authenticated `GET /api/info`.
- Pairing codes are redeemed exactly once; never retry a redeem automatically.
- A 401 on a saved profile is surfaced as `OpenCodeError.Unauthorized` and
  leads the user to re-pair or update the password. Network failures stay
  retryable and never delete a profile.
- Removing the active server activates the next saved server or returns to the
  connect flow.
- Never log, toast, screenshot or put in analytics: passwords, tokens, pairing
  codes or full pairing links. Show only scheme/host/port.

Load `android-security` for storage, clipboard and camera rules and
`android-opencode-api` for HTTP client changes.

## Verification

Cover pairing success, expired/used code, wrong password, unreachable host,
switching servers while a stream is open, removing the active server and app
restart with a saved server.

# Android Benchmarks

`android/benchmark` holds the automated performance tests. They drive the real app
through UiAutomator and read the system trace, so a number comes from the same code a
user runs. Use them to get the "before" of a performance change and the "after" from the
same command. `android-performance` owns diagnosis and fixes; this skill owns measuring.

## What Is Measured

- **Build:** the app's `benchmark` build type: release code and R8, not debuggable,
  debug-signed, application id suffix `.benchmark`, so it installs beside the real app.
  Never measure a debug build: it is several times slower and misleads.
- **Data:** the offline demo (`USE_FAKE_DATA` is true in this build type). Runs need no
  server, always show the same sessions, and the demo has sessions at work. Do not point
  a benchmark at a real server.
- **Tests** (`benchmark/src/main/kotlin/.../benchmarks`):
  - `IdleWorkBenchmark`: screens left alone for 10 s; `idleFrameCount` and `idleCpuMs`
    from `IdleWorkMetric` (frames and CPU of the app process in the trace).
  - `StartupBenchmark`: cold start to the session list, not compiled and with the
    shipped profile.
  - `SessionListScrollBenchmark`: frame timings while flinging the list.

## Which Numbers To Trust

- **Counts and sums compare everywhere:** `idleFrameCount`, `idleCpuMs` relative to the
  idle reference, `frameCount`. A still screen produces about no frames on any machine;
  one infinite animation produces the display rate (about 600 in 10 s at 60 Hz).
- **Timings are relative on an emulator:** startup and frame durations depend on the
  host and its load. Compare a change with its baseline on the same emulator in the same
  session; never quote them as what users get. Absolute numbers need a physical device.
- A benchmark may **gate** (fail a build) only on counts. Timings are reported and
  compared over several runs, not asserted against a fixed threshold.
- The emulator error is suppressed in `benchmark/build.gradle.kts` on purpose; this is
  what makes local and CI runs possible, not a statement that emulator timings are valid.

## Rules

- One emulator, nothing else heavy running, the same device for before and after.
- Stop Mobile MCP's UiAutomator client first (`adb shell pkill -f mobilecli`): two
  UiAutomator clients cannot hold the device.
- Every test starts from a fresh process (`restartDemo()`), so one test never inherits
  the screen of another.
- Find views by `testTag` (exposed as resource ids); add a tag in the app rather than
  matching visible text.
- A new scenario is a new `@Test` in the class that owns the metric; keep the measured
  block to the thing measured and put navigation in `setupBlock`.
- Report the scenario, device, build, metric medians with min and max, and what was not
  measured. A single run is not a result.
- Keep versions in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. CI compiles the benchmark sources
  (`:benchmark:compileBenchmarkKotlin`) and never runs them; no Baseline Profile plugin is
  configured. Running in CI or adding the plugin is its own task.

Commands, reading the results, and running on a phone are in
[references/running.md](references/running.md).

# Android Compose And MVI

Give each state value one lowest responsible owner. Keep application wiring at
the route/host boundary and rendering in plain, previewable composables.

## Route And Screen Split

A thin `XxxRoute` composable may:

- Resolve a ViewModel through Koin.
- Collect `state` with `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`.
- Collect effects through `CollectEffect`.
- Translate navigation, permission, activity-result, and environment callbacks.

It must not contain business rules. A screen/content composable receives
immutable `State`, an `onEvent` callback, and UI/environment callbacks when
needed. It may own genuinely local framework state such as scroll, focus,
animation, sheet state, or an interaction source.

```kotlin
val viewModel: SessionsViewModel = koinViewModel()
val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()

CollectEffect(viewModel.effect) { effect -> /* navigation or transient UI */ }
SessionsScreen(state = state, onEvent = viewModel::onEvent)
```

Do not pass ViewModels, repositories, network clients, NavController, or Koin
through the rendering tree.

Screens are Compose Multiplatform code in `commonMain`: `koinViewModel()` comes from
`org.koin.compose.viewmodel`, `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`/`LocalLifecycleOwner` from
`androidx.lifecycle.compose`, back handling from `OcBackHandler`, clipboard from
`rememberTextClipboard()`. `LocalContext`, Activity result launchers and other
platform APIs stay behind `expect` composables or interfaces
(`kmp-platform-boundaries`).

## MVI Contract

- Define `Event`, immutable `State`, and one-shot `Effect` types.
- New ViewModels extend `BaseViewModel<State, Event, Effect>` and expose one
  `onEvent` entry point.
- Use `updateState`, `currentState`, `sendEffect`, and `viewModelScope`.
- Keep durable truth in State: data, validation, loading, saved outcomes, and
  errors that must survive recreation or recollection.
- Use Effect only for transient imperative commands: navigation, toast,
  snackbar, focus, permission, picker, or external activity launch.
- Never encode business truth exclusively as an Effect.
- Preserve existing content during refresh; reserve full-screen loading for the
  initial load.

## Compose Effects

- Use `LaunchedEffect` for suspend work tied to composition and semantic keys.
- Use `DisposableEffect` only when registering a resource that needs cleanup.
- Use `SideEffect` only to publish successful composition state externally.
- Use `rememberCoroutineScope` for UI-triggered work owned by that composable,
  not to move repository business work into UI.
- Use `rememberUpdatedState` only when a long-lived effect needs current values
  without restarting.
- Clean up listeners, players, sensors, launchers, and controllers at their
  actual lifecycle owner.

## Design System And Semantics

- Prefer existing `Oc*` components from `core:ui`; inspect their APIs before
  rebuilding a Material equivalent. `docs/design-system.md` lists tokens and
  components.
- Colors come from `OcTheme` (OpenCode V2 tokens: backgrounds, text, borders,
  state and agent colors) or the derived `MaterialTheme.colorScheme`; never
  hard-code colors in features.
- Typography: Inter for UI text, IBM Plex Mono for code, tool names, paths and
  commands.
- Use the `OcSpacing` scale. Hard-coded dimensions are acceptable for intrinsic
  icon sizes, touch targets and other values that are not spacing tokens.
- Use bottom sheets for pickers and create flows; reserve dialogs for
  confirmation or destructive actions.
- Give interactive controls stable `testTag` values. Use semantics for behavior
  and accessibility; do not rely on visible localized text as automation ID.
- Use stable keys in lazy collections.

## Edge To Edge And IME

- The root app shell owns system insets. A nested `Scaffold` sets
  `contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets(0)` unless it is deliberately the inset
  owner.
- Apply `innerPadding`, then consume it before applying child IME handling.
- Put `imePadding()` or equivalent handling at the lowest container that must
  move above the keyboard. Do not stack it at multiple ancestors.
- Apply list insets through `contentPadding` when content should scroll behind
  system bars rather than padding and clipping the whole list.
- Verify keyboard-open and system-bar states on a real runtime after changes.

## Text Input Visibility

- Use the `Oc*` text field components for single-line and multiline input; the
  chat composer is the reference multiline field.
- Every editable multiline field must have a finite visible height. Keep
  `maxLines` finite and greater than or equal to `minLines` so the field scrolls
  internally and Compose keeps the cursor and newly entered text visible.
- Do not use `Int.MAX_VALUE` for an editable text area's `maxLines` inside a
  scrolling form. An unbounded field grows with old content instead of providing
  a stable viewport for current input.
- Put long fields inside an IME-aware scroll owner. Rely on Compose's automatic
  nested scrolling between `TextField` and the parent; add custom
  `BringIntoViewRequester` logic only when runtime evidence shows the standard
  behavior is insufficient.
- When `minLines` exceeds the default maximum, set an explicit finite
  `maxLines` at least as large as `minLines`.

## Streaming Transcript

- Live events are applied to State with `TranscriptReducer`; composables only
  render the resulting `Message`/`Part` list.
- Key transcript items by message ID and parts by `Part.key`.
- Parse Markdown through the shared parse cache so finished messages are parsed
  once and only the streaming message re-parses.
- Auto-scroll only while the user is at the bottom; otherwise show a
  "jump to latest" control.

## Performance Handoff

Do not add `remember`, `derivedStateOf`, `@Stable`, `@Immutable`, or immutable
collection wrappers as generic cleanup. When recomposition, jank, or stability
is the actual task, load `android-performance`, gather evidence, and return here
only for the resulting UI ownership/edit.

## Verification

- Plain screen composables should be testable from supplied State.
- Verify loading, empty, error, content, and relevant form states.
- For text input changes, type beyond the visible line limit and verify that the
  cursor, latest text, selection, and relevant actions remain visible with the
  keyboard open.
- For other layout changes, inspect keyboard, scrolling, sheet/dialog, and
  affected adaptive states.
- Load `android-localization-accessibility` when copy, semantics, focus, RTL,
  font scale, or adaptive behavior changes.

name: android-coroutines
description: Use for opencode-mobile coroutine scope ownership, the shared /api/event stream and reconnection, suspend APIs, Flow/StateFlow/SharedFlow/Channel, cancellation, dispatchers, background work, runBlocking, or asynchronous error handling.
---

# Android Coroutines And Flow

Async work has one explicit lifecycle owner. Prefer structured concurrency and
suspending APIs over hidden fire-and-forget work.

## Scope Ownership

- `viewModelScope` translates non-suspending UI events into async work.
- `rememberCoroutineScope` is valid for UI work owned by a composable.
- Repositories and data sources normally expose `suspend` or cold `Flow` APIs;
  the caller owns cancellation.
- A stored `CoroutineScope` is a review signal. Keep it only when the class has
  a documented lifecycle, cancellation method, error policy, and restart rules.
- Android services may own a service scope, but cancel it in the corresponding
  lifecycle callback.
- The app-scoped `CoroutineScope` registered in `dataModule` owns the shared
  event stream (`stateIn`/`shareIn` with `WhileSubscribed`). It pauses while the
  app is in the background and restarts when the active server changes.
- Reconnection uses bounded exponential backoff and stops when there are no
  collectors; never reconnect in a tight loop.
- Use WorkManager or a platform service for work that must outlive the current
  UI/process contract; do not simulate durability with an ad-hoc scope.

Never use `GlobalScope`. Never create a new scope per call.

## Cancellation And Errors

- Never swallow `CancellationException`.
- Broad catches around suspend calls must rethrow cancellation before mapping or
  logging other failures.
- Do not use `runCatching` around suspend work unless cancellation is explicitly
  preserved.
- Callbacks from HTTP engines or platform APIs may run in another coroutine or
  thread: bridge them with `channelFlow { send() }` or `callbackFlow`, never
  `flow { emit() }` (Ktor's Darwin engine runs `execute {}` in another coroutine).
- In common code import `kotlinx.coroutines.IO` for `Dispatchers.IO`; Objective-C
  callbacks hop to the main queue before touching UI state.
- Catch at the layer that can add meaning: retry, map to a domain result, update
  UI state, or log with useful non-sensitive context.
- Avoid silently converting unexpected failures to `null` or an empty list.
- Log a failure once at the owning boundary. Preserve the throwable/cause for
  diagnostics but expose a typed, localized-safe message to UI.
- Never log passwords, pairing tokens or codes, Authorization headers, prompts,
  transcripts, tool output, file contents, or raw server bodies.

## Dispatchers

- Inject dispatchers only where tests or ownership genuinely benefit.
- Use `Dispatchers.IO` for blocking file, socket, archive, or legacy API work.
- Use `Dispatchers.Default` for genuinely CPU-heavy work.
- Do not wrap already non-blocking/main-safe suspend APIs in IO reflexively.
- Production `runBlocking`, especially during application startup, requires an
  explicit blocking contract and performance evidence; prefer suspendable or
  asynchronous initialization.

## Flow Modeling

- Never expose `MutableStateFlow` or `MutableSharedFlow` outside its owner.
- Use `StateFlow` for durable observable state.
- Use Flow for streams; use suspend functions for one-shot work.
- Use the project `Channel`-backed Effect only for transient UI commands that
  may be lost when no UI collector exists.
- Durable results and business truth belong in State or persistent storage.
- Collect Android UI state with `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`.
- Document sharing start/stop behavior when using `stateIn` or `shareIn`.

## Review Checklist

- Who cancels every launched job?
- Can a newer request supersede an older one, and is the old job cancelled?
- Does a stop/release method cancel pending network/file work too?
- Can cancellation be mistaken for a user-visible error?
- Is shared mutable state confined or synchronized without blocking threads?
- Can tests advance virtual time deterministically?

name: android-data-boundaries
description: Use when designing or changing opencode-mobile repository interfaces in core:domain, their implementations in core:data, local stores, SharedPreferences schemas, OpenCodeError mapping, domain mapping, or transcript reconciliation with TranscriptReducer.
---

# Android Data Boundaries

Repositories and stores present small, main-safe contracts to ViewModels. They
hide transport, persistence, dispatcher, and generated-model details while
preserving cancellation and actionable failures.

## Repository Contracts

- Use `suspend` for one-shot work and cold `Flow` for streams.
- Return `core:domain` models rather than generated API models, Ktor
  responses, cursors, Android controllers, or mutable storage objects.
- Choose one failure contract per cohesive API: typed result, nullable absence,
  or exception. Do not mix meanings for convenience.
- Distinguish not-found/empty from transport, authorization, validation, and
  unexpected failures.
- Keep public methods main-safe; isolate genuinely blocking file/socket work on
  the appropriate dispatcher.
- Repository interfaces live in `core:domain/Repositories.kt` because features
  depend only on that module; implementations live in `core:data`.
- One-shot calls return `Result<T>` whose failures are `OpenCodeError`.

Load `android-opencode-api` or `android-security` when those systems own the
transport-specific decision.

## Transcript Reconciliation

- The server is the source of truth for messages. Live events update the
  transcript optimistically through the pure `TranscriptReducer`.
- Transcripts are mirrored in a Room cache (`core/data/cache`), keyed by saved server and
  session, storing the server wire JSON (`MessageCodec`) so mapping changes apply to cached
  history. The chat shows `ChatRepository.cachedMessages` first, then `messages` syncs.
- Session and project lists are also cached per saved server in Room (`ListCache`, domain
  JSON via `SessionListCodec`): shown first on start and server switch, refreshed after each
  load, cleared with drafts and transcripts when the server is removed.
- Newest first: the cache holds the newest part of a transcript (at most 1000 entries) plus
  `olderCursor` (server cursor to the history before it; null when complete or trimmed).
  `messages` syncs the newest part; `olderMessages` loads one older page (200) and the chat
  calls it until null, prepending to what is shown. Past the cap, pages are shown but not
  stored, and the cursor to the rest is kept in memory by `RemoteChatRepository`.
- List endpoints decode item by item (`TolerantPages`): unknown message or part variants are
  skipped, never failing the whole page; paging compares the server's raw item count.
- Sync is incremental: the anchor is the newest entry such that it and everything older
  are settled (`MessageCodec.isSettled`: no running step, shell or compaction). Pages are
  fetched newest-first (first page 50) until the anchor; everything after it is replaced.
  Without a usable anchor (none cached, not found, undecodable cache) the cache restarts
  from the newest page of 50.
- The sessions list calls `prefetch` for its 5 most recent sessions: sessions not cached
  yet store their last 2 messages, so they open with content.
- The cache is disposable (destructive migrations), keeps the 50 most recently synced
  sessions per server and is cleared when a server is removed.
- Reload messages after `ServerEvent.Connected` (reconnect), step end, execution
  end and structural changes, then `TranscriptReducer.merge` keeps queued prompts
  and the live assistant message that the server has not persisted yet.
- System instructions are dropped in mapping. `idle` and `synthetic` messages are kept
  as `Message.Idle`/`Message.Synthetic`: they are not rendered but define turns.
- A turn is one server execution, as in the OpenCode TUI: from the first user or
  synthetic message after the previous idle up to the next idle. Prompts steered or
  queued while running belong to it. Footer duration, tok/s and cost are computed over
  the whole execution; sessions without idle markers fall back to one turn per prompt.
- Live `session.execution.*` events insert the same idle message the server stores
  (event id with `evt_` replaced by `msg_`), so live and reloaded turns agree.
- Revert follows the TUI: `revert.stage(messageId)` hides that message and everything
  after it (cut in `ChatViewModel.visibleMessages`, not in the cache) and returns its text
  to the composer; `revert.clear` restores; the next prompt first calls `revert.commit`.
  `session.revert.*` events map to `ServerEvent.RevertChanged`.

## Prompt Input

- Attachments are `PromptAttachment` URIs: uploads are `data:` URIs read by
  `AttachmentReader` (bounded to 10 MB, photos downscaled to 2048 px JPEG); `@` mentions
  are `file://<session directory>/<path>` with the mention text. The mention position is
  computed from the final prompt text in `PromptMapping`; deleted mentions are dropped.
- `/name args` runs `session.command` when `name` is a server command; `/undo` and
  `/redo` are handled locally; anything else is sent as a plain prompt.
- Forms (agent questions) come from `session.form.list` and `form.*` events. Hidden
  fields become `Form.presetAnswers`; replies include presets plus answers of visible
  fields (`Form.reply`), with `when` conditions evaluated in the domain.

## Local Stores

- Settings and drafts use multiplatform-settings `Settings` (`SettingsStore`,
  `DraftsStore` qualifiers): `SharedPreferencesSettings` over the existing `settings` and
  `drafts` files on Android, `NSUserDefaultsSettings` suites on iOS. Saved servers use
  `ServerStore` (EncryptedSharedPreferences / Keychain). Keep file names, keys and JSON
  schemas unchanged: they are read by upgrading installs.
- Room is Room KMP: DAOs are `suspend`, the database has `@ConstructedBy` with the
  generated `expect object`, Android keeps the framework SQLite database
  `message-cache.db`, iOS uses `BundledSQLiteDriver` in Caches. Catch
  `androidx.sqlite.SQLiteException`. Do not adopt Room 3 during unrelated work.

- Treat preference/file keys and serialized payloads as a persisted schema.
- Define defaults, missing/corrupt-value behavior, version/migration needs, and
  whether each value may be backed up.
- Store the minimum necessary data. Private drafts, auth material, transcripts,
  and temporary files require explicit retention and cleanup policy.
- Do not expose mutable SharedPreferences or serializer state to feature code.
- Writes that must be durable before the next operation must not rely on an
  asynchronous persistence call without acknowledging that contract.

## Files And Cache

- Name the owner of every cache/temp file and when it is deleted.
- Prefer bounded streaming over reading an untrusted content URI fully into
  memory.
- Validate scheme, MIME type, display name, declared/actual size, and required
  seekability before expensive work.
- Close cursors, streams, HTTP responses, and file descriptors on every path.
- Never log authorization headers, private file contents, prompts or raw
  server response bodies.

## Mapping And Errors

- Keep protocol-to-domain mapping near the data source/repository.
- Unknown generated enum members need a deliberate fallback or typed failure.
- User messages are localized at the UI boundary; repositories retain typed
  meaning and diagnostic causes without exposing secrets.
- Broad catches around suspend calls rethrow `CancellationException`.

## Testing

Test mapping, corrupt local data, missing values, migration/default behavior,
blocking dispatcher boundaries, cancellation, oversized/malformed files, cache
cleanup, and every typed error branch relevant to consumers.

description: Use for opencode-mobile AGP 9, Gradle Kotlin DSL, Kotlin Multiplatform targets and source sets (com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library), Compose Multiplatform resources configuration, KSP per target, the version catalog, module graph, SDK/toolchains, dependencies, or build types.

# Android And KMP Gradle

Gradle 9.8.1, AGP 9.4.1, Kotlin 2.4.21, Compose Multiplatform 1.12.2, compile SDK 37,
target SDK 36, min SDK 26, JVM target 11, Gradle daemon on JDK 21. iOS targets are
`iosArm64` and `iosSimulatorArm64`. There are no product flavors; app build types are
`debug` (application ID suffix `.debug`), `release` and `benchmark` (release code, debug
key, suffix `.benchmark`, offline demo data; measured by the `:benchmark` test module).

## Module Shapes

- `:app` is the only `com.android.application` (built-in Kotlin, Android only).
  `:core:testing` stays a plain `com.android.library` for JVM test helpers.
- Every other module is a KMP library: `kotlin.multiplatform` +
  `android.kotlin.multiplatform.library`, configured in `kotlin { android { ... } }`
  (namespace, `compileSdk`, `minSdk`, `compilerOptions.jvmTarget`), plus
  `iosArm64()` and `iosSimulatorArm64()`. Compose modules add `compose.multiplatform`
  and `kotlin.compose`. Use `android/core/mvi/build.gradle.kts` as the template.
- Source sets: `commonMain`, `androidMain`, `iosMain`, `commonTest`,
  `androidHostTest` (enable with `withHostTest {}`); dependencies go in
  `sourceSets { xxx.dependencies { } }`, never in a top-level `dependencies {}`
  except KSP and `androidRuntimeClasspath` tooling.
- Modules with Compose resources need `androidResources { enable = true }` inside
  `kotlin { android { } }` (otherwise Android fails at runtime with
  `MissingResourceException`) and a `compose.resources { packageOfResClass = "<namespace>.resources" }`
  block; only `core:ui` sets `publicResClass = true`.
- KSP (Room) is added per target: `add("kspAndroid", ...)`, `add("kspIosArm64", ...)`,
  `add("kspIosSimulatorArm64", ...)`.
- KMP libraries have no `BuildConfig` and a single variant: pass build values from
  the app (`AppInfo`) or use `Platform.isDebugBinary` on iOS.
- The iOS framework (`Shared`, static) is declared only in `:shared`.

## Rules

- Kotlin DSL and `gradle/libs.versions.toml` only. Compose Multiplatform artifacts use
  the `compose-*`, `jb-lifecycle-*`, `jb-navigation-*` catalog entries; on Android they
  resolve to the AndroidX artifacts. Material 3 is pinned to the CMP version that maps
  to the AndroidX release the app used (1.9.0 → 1.4.0) and AndroidX navigation is kept
  at its own patch level in `:shared` `androidMain`.
- Do not add `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android`, `androidTarget {}`, legacy
  `com.android.library` for KMP modules, `kotlinOptions` or legacy variant APIs.
- Inspect the catalog, the target build file and one similar module before adding
  dependencies or plugins. Do not bump a major dependency, SDK, Kotlin, AGP, CMP or
  Gradle during unrelated work.
- Module build files are explicit; no convention plugins. The only cross-project
  logic is the root alias that registers `testDebugUnitTest` → `testAndroidHostTest`
  in KMP modules, so one test command covers every module.

## Module Graph

```text
app -> shared -> feature:{connect,sessions,chat,settings,terminal,files} -> core:{ui,mvi,domain}
app -> core:data -> core:network -> core:api (generated)
shared (iosMain) -> core:data
```

Features never depend on `:app`, `:shared`, other features, `core:network` or `core:api`.
`core:api` contains only generated sources; its build file is hand-written.

## Verification

- While iterating: `./gradlew :<module>:compileAndroidMain
  :<module>:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64 :<module>:testDebugUnitTest`.
- Before finishing broad changes: `./gradlew spotlessCheck testDebugUnitTest
  :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug compileKotlinIosArm64 compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`.
- Release/R8 changes: `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease` and a smoke test of the release
  APK (pairing, chat, event stream). Libraries ship their own keep rules.
- iOS framework linking and slow native builds: `kmp-ios`,
  `kotlin-tooling-native-build-performance`.

# Android Koin

Follow the project's Koin DSL. Do not migrate to annotations or a compiler plugin
during unrelated work.

## Registration Ownership

- `core/data/.../di/DataModule.kt` (`dataModule`) registers repositories, the
  network client cache, the shared event stream and the app-scoped
  `CoroutineScope`.
- `shared/.../SharedModule.kt` (`sharedModule(appInfo)`) registers ViewModels for both
  apps; `app/.../AppModule.kt` (`appModule`) includes it and adds Android-only
  notifications. `dataModule` includes the platform bindings of `platformDataModule`
  (`core/data/src/{android,ios}Main/.../di/`).
- `OpenCodeApplication` starts Koin with `dataModules() + appModule`; on iOS
  `MainViewController()` starts it once with `dataModule` and `sharedModule`.
- Use `viewModelOf(::Type)` for ordinary constructor injection and
  `viewModel { params -> Type(params.get(), get()) }` for runtime parameters such
  as a session ID.
- Use `single { }` only for intentional app-scoped instances; `factory` for
  short-lived objects whose caller owns lifetime.

Bind implementations under the exact interface type consumers request, for
example `single<SessionRepository> { DefaultSessionRepository(get()) }`.

## Consumption

- Resolve route ViewModels with `koinViewModel()` and pass parameters with
  `parametersOf(...)`.
- Use `koinInject()` only for intentionally shared app-scoped infrastructure.
- Do not call `get()` from business code or pass Koin through feature layers.

Read `references/module-verification.md` when adding Koin verification tests.

name: android-localization-accessibility
description: Use when changing opencode-mobile user-visible strings (Compose Multiplatform resources, English default, Italian values-it), plurals, dates, numbers, units, content descriptions, semantics, TalkBack, focus, RTL, font scale, adaptive layout, window sizes, or accessibility tests.

# Android Localization, Accessibility, And Adaptive UI

User-visible copy and semantics are release contracts, not decoration. New UI
must work with locale changes, TalkBack, RTL, large fonts, keyboard/focus, and
the window sizes relevant to the feature.

## Localized Content

- Put new user-visible static strings in the owning module's Compose Multiplatform
  resources (`src/commonMain/composeResources/values*/strings.xml`) and use
  `org.jetbrains.compose.resources.stringResource`/`pluralStringResource` with the
  module's generated `Res` (`core:ui` strings via `...core.ui.resources.Res as UiRes`).
  Outside composition (effects, snackbars) use `UiText.Resource` and the suspend
  `asString()`/`getString`. Only `:app` notification text stays in Android `res/`.
- Compose resources differ from Android: placeholders must be positional (`%1$s`,
  `%2$d`; `$s` and `$d` are interchangeable and nothing else is substituted, so
  pre-format decimals in code); write `'`, `"`, `@`, `?` and `%` unescaped; `\n`,
  `\t` and `\uXXXX` still work. Locale folders keep Android names (`values-pt-rBR`,
  `values-b+zh+Hans`).
- Do not localize `testTag`, route identifiers, server enum values, agent or
  model IDs, tool names, storage keys, or protocol fields.
- Every new string gets an English default and an Italian translation.
- Map server/exception details to safe user-facing resource messages; keep the
  diagnostic cause separate.
- Use locale-aware date, time, number, decimal, percentage, currency, and unit
  formatting through the `core:ui` helpers (`formatInteger`, `relativeTime`, platform
  date formatting actuals). Do not concatenate units or implement plurals with
  string logic.
- Notification/channel text is user-visible and follows the same rules.
- Migrate existing hard-coded strings incrementally in the screen being changed;
  do not block a feature on a repository-wide translation migration.

## Semantics And Interaction

- Prefer native Material semantics, then add only missing role, selected/state
  description, heading, error, live-region, traversal, or custom-action data.
- Decorative icons/images use `contentDescription = null`; meaningful icon-only
  actions have a localized accessible name.
- Avoid nested independently clickable controls that announce or execute the
  same action twice.
- Keep touch targets at least 48 dp unless a documented platform exception
  applies.
- Error, loading, selected, expanded, checked, and progress states must be
  discoverable without color alone.
- Keep keyboard and D-pad focus order predictable; focus requests belong to the
  UI owner and use a justified Compose effect lifecycle.
- Editable multiline fields must use a finite viewport and remain internally
  scrollable so the cursor, selection, and newly entered text stay visible with
  the IME open. Test by entering more lines than the visible limit, not only by
  focusing a short value.

Automation identity and accessibility are separate: every interactive control
still receives a stable `testTag`, while tests assert semantics and behavior.

## Adaptive Layout

- Define what compact, medium, and expanded mean for the affected screen before
  adding raw width checks.
- Prefer constraints/window-size information at a layout owner; do not scatter
  device-model or orientation checks through leaves.
- Preserve readable content widths, reachable actions, list/detail ownership,
  system insets, and navigation behavior across resizing and rotation.
- Avoid adopting Navigation 3 or SDK 37 alpha APIs as an incidental adaptive fix.

## Verification

`bun test tools/locales.test.ts` (repository root) checks keys, placeholders and
escaping in every locale. On iOS, VoiceOver uses accessibility labels (test tags are
not exposed); check shared UI changes on the simulator as well (`kmp-ios`).

Check the affected UI with TalkBack semantics, 1.5x font scale, RTL where layout
direction matters, compact and expanded widths, keyboard/focus behavior, and
light/dark contrast when colors change. Add focused Compose tests for semantics
and callbacks; use screenshots only for visual contracts.

# Android Navigation

The app uses Navigation Compose 2.9 with `@Serializable` route types. Do not
migrate to Navigation 3 during feature work.

## Navigation Owners

- `:app` owns the root `NavHost`, the route types and the start decision:
  no active server -> Connect, otherwise Sessions.
- Feature modules expose `XxxRoute(...)` composables with navigation callbacks;
  they never receive a `NavController`.
- Screen composables emit `onEvent` only; navigation is a ViewModel Effect or a
  route callback.

## Route Wiring

- Resolve route ViewModels with `koinViewModel()`; pass arguments such as the
  session ID with `parametersOf(...)`.
- Collect State lifecycle-aware and Effects with `CollectEffect` in the route.
- Make "screen shown" events idempotent; a destination may re-enter.

## Back Stack Decisions

- Successful connect replaces Connect with Sessions (pop Connect inclusive).
- Removing or switching the active server to none clears the stack back to Connect.
- Opening a session pushes Chat; creating a session navigates to its Chat and
  removes the creation sheet.
- Settings is pushed from Sessions; Back returns to Sessions.
- Do not use `popUpTo(0)`, `launchSingleTop` or state restoration without naming
  the intended history behavior.

## Adaptive Layout

On expanded widths a list-detail layout may show Sessions and Chat together.
Keep the same route types so phone and wide layouts share ViewModels and back
semantics.

## Verification

Test entry, back from Chat and Settings, connect -> sessions replacement,
server removal, process recreation where relevant, and the wide layout when
touched.

name: android-opencode-api
description: Use for the generated OpenCode V2 Kotlin client in opencode-mobile/android/core/api, the Ktor HTTP client, Basic auth transport, the /api/event SSE stream, mapping generated models to domain models, or regenerating the client with tools/api-gen (bun run generate).

# Android OpenCode API

The OpenCode server owns the contract. The app consumes a generated client and
maps it to domain models at one boundary.

## Ownership

```text
feature ViewModel
  -> repository interface (core:domain)
  -> repository implementation (core:data)
  -> OpenCode client + mappers (core:network)
  -> generated Ktor APIs and models (core:api, Kotlin Multiplatform)
```

- `core:api` is produced by openapi-generator 7.22 (`kotlin`, `kotlinx_serialization`)
  from `api/openapi.json` plus event schemas from npm `@opencode/schema`, in two passes:
  models from `jvm-retrofit2` (sealed union serializers, plain kotlinx-serialization code)
  and API classes plus their Ktor infrastructure from `multiplatform`. Everything lives in
  `commonMain`, is committed and never edited by hand.
- `core:network` (Kotlin Multiplatform) owns Ktor client construction (OkHttp engine on
  Android, Darwin on iOS), authentication headers, SSE reading, error mapping and
  generated-to-domain mappers.
- Features never see generated types, Ktor or HTTP status codes.

## Regenerating

```bash
cd tools/api-gen
bun run refresh   # new server version: download spec, pin @opencode/schema, regenerate
bun run generate  # regenerate from committed spec
bun run check     # CI/verification: committed output is current
```

- Need a new API area? Add its tag to `KEEP_TAGS` in
  `tools/api-gen/src/prepare-spec.ts` and regenerate.
- A generator limitation is fixed by a minimal, commented preprocessing step in
  `prepare-spec.ts`, never by editing generated files.
- After regenerating, build `:core:network` and `:core:data` and run their tests;
  fixture tests catch contract drift.

Read `references/generator.md` before changing preprocessing or generator flags.

## Generated Shapes

- Responses usually wrap payloads: `{ data: ... }`, lists add `cursor`.
- REST unions (for example `SessionMessageInfo`, assistant content, tool state)
  are sealed interfaces of `*Value` wrappers holding the concrete class.
- The event union is `OpenCodeEvent` with `*Wrapper` members keyed by the wire
  `type` (`session.text.delta` -> `SessiontextdeltaWrapper`).
- Location-scoped endpoints take `locationDirectory` (`location[directory]`).
- Message pages are limited to 200 items; follow `cursor.next`.
- Enums use `enumUnknownDefaultCase=false`: decoding fails loudly on unknown
  discriminator values, so union decoding stays unambiguous. Map defensively in
  `core:network` and drop unknown event types.

## Transport Rules

- One Ktor client per active server, derived from a shared base client (one engine and
  connection pool); authentication is HTTP Basic `opencode:<secret>` sent as a default
  header. Bearer is not accepted.
- Generated calls return `HttpResponse<T>` and never throw on HTTP status; wrap them in
  `awaitBody` / `awaitSuccess`. Message and session pages are decoded by
  `TolerantPagesConverter`, which skips items this client cannot decode.
- `/api/event` is a never-ending SSE stream. The server sends a `:` heartbeat comment
  every 15 s, so the stream client uses a 45 s read timeout to detect dead connections;
  the call ends with the collector and comments are ignored. A 401 sets
  `ConnectionState.Unauthorized` and stops retrying until the server or credentials change.
- Debug logging must redact `Authorization` and never log request bodies (they
  contain prompts) or pairing responses.
- Map failures to `OpenCodeError` at the network boundary: 401 -> Unauthorized,
  IO -> Unreachable, pairing 4xx -> PairingFailed, otherwise Server with `_tag`.

For credentials and pairing load `android-auth-session`; for stream lifecycle
load `android-coroutines`.

# Android Performance

No performance optimization without evidence. Measure one user-visible
transition, change one axis, and measure the same transition again.

## Route The Problem

- Compose recomposition/skipping: compiler reports and recomposition evidence.
- Frame jank, CPU, scheduling, startup, IO, binder, or system interaction:
  Perfetto/System Trace.
- Release shrinking, missing classes, or APK size: R8 mapping/usage/configuration
  analysis.
- Critical startup/journey regression, or a screen that keeps drawing while idle:
  the Macrobenchmark module (`android-benchmarks` skill) for the before and after;
  Baseline Profiles when justified.
- Memory/resource lifetime: profiler/heap evidence plus explicit lifecycle
  ownership review.

Do not infer a Compose problem from a slow screen without a trace.

Use `references/compose-diagnostics.md` for Compose-specific diagnosis and
`references/perfetto.md` for trace capture/analysis.

## Compose

- Kotlin 2.2 strong skipping changes old stability assumptions.
- Do not add `@Stable`, `@Immutable`, `remember`, `derivedStateOf`, immutable
  collections, or callback wrappers by default.
- Distinguish actual data changes, unstable instance churn, State reads in the
  wrong phase, and cross-phase back-writing.
- False stability annotations can produce stale UI.

## Compose Multiplatform Resources

`stringResource`/`Font` from Compose resources resolve synchronously on first
composition; many distinct strings in a lazy list item can cost frame time. Measure
(trace or macrobenchmark against the previous build) before restructuring; hoist
repeated lookups out of list items only with evidence.

## Startup

Inspect synchronous work in `Application`, Activity creation, Koin graph startup,
network discovery, disk reads, class loading, and main-thread blocking. Do not
move work to a background scope merely to hide it; define when consumers may use
the initialized dependency and how failures/retries behave.

## R8 And Release

- Inspect AGP version and current release configuration first.
- Release builds use R8 (`isMinifyEnabled`, `isShrinkResources`); libraries ship
  their own keep rules and `app/proguard-rules.pro` only fills gaps.
- AGP 9.4.1 includes the standalone R8 analyzer task (added in AGP 9.3); verify
  its output against the release build before acting on it.
- Remove or narrow keep rules only with release-build and runtime evidence.
- Validate kotlinx-serialization (generated API models and union serializers),
  Ktor and kotlinx-serialization, Koin, CameraX and the markdown renderer after R8 changes.

## Report

Record the scenario, build/device, measurement tool, baseline, change,
after result, and residual uncertainty. Do not claim an improvement from source
inspection alone.

# Android Runtime Verification

A successful build is necessary but not sufficient for behavior or visual
changes. Match verification depth to risk.

## Workflow

1. Run the module tests required by `android/AGENTS.md`.
2. Use a running emulator (`adb devices` reports its serial) and set
   `adb -s <serial> reverse tcp:4096 tcp:4096`.
3. Make sure an OpenCode server listens on host port 4096
   (`opencode api get /api/info`).
4. From `android/`: `ANDROID_SERIAL=<serial> ./gradlew :app:installDebug`
   (application ID `io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.debug`).
5. Bring the existing task forward without force-stopping:
   `adb -s <serial> shell am start -n io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.debug/io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile.MainActivity`.
6. If no server is saved, connect to `http://localhost:4096` by pairing: create a
   code with `opencode pair --url http://localhost:4096` or `opencode api post /api/pair`,
   and type it with `adb shell input text` — never print it in reports or
   screenshots.
7. Navigate by stable testTag/resource ID with Mobile MCP, Maestro or ADB.
8. Exercise the changed interaction and inspect the rendered result in light and
   dark theme; check font scale 1.3 and keyboard-open states for layout changes.
9. Check Logcat after the interaction:
   `adb -s <serial> logcat -d -v threadtime AndroidRuntime:E '*:S'`.

Do not send prompts in real user sessions. To test prompting, create a session in a
disposable scratch directory with a cheap model (for example
`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`) and a trivial prompt.

## Verification Depth

- Visual token/icon/spacing: load and inspect the exact state.
- Interaction/state: perform the action and verify resulting State/UI.
- Navigation: traverse entry and return paths.
- Streaming: watch text, reasoning and tool rows update live, then reconcile.
- Connection: pairing, wrong password, server stopped, reconnect.
- Insets/layout: system bars, scrolling, keyboard open, sheet/dialog.

If verification is impossible, name the blocker and separate verified facts from
assumptions.

## iOS

Shared UI or iOS-specific changes are also verified on the iOS simulator on the Mac;
follow `kmp-ios` (build, install, DeviceKit automation, crash reports).

## Final Evidence

Report the exact checks, emulator serial, server version, screen, interaction,
screenshots taken (without secrets) and any state not verified.

# Android Security

Treat every scanned QR, pasted link, intent and server payload as untrusted.

## Components And Intents

- Only the launcher activity, the widget receiver and the share menu entry
  (`ShareActivity`, which can be disabled in Settings) are exported. New activities,
  services, receivers and providers default to `android:exported="false"`.
- Shared content is untrusted: `ShareIntents` accepts only plain text and images,
  bounds the text, refuses `file:` URIs and this app's own providers, and the images
  are copied at once into app-private no-backup storage. Never log shared content.
- Validate `onCreate` and `onNewIntent` paths for the `singleTop` activity.
- Do not add deep links that accept pairing codes from other apps without an
  explicit decision; codes grant full server access.

## Network

- OpenCode servers are self-hosted on a LAN or VPN and usually plain HTTP, so
  cleartext is allowed by `network_security_config.xml`. Show the scheme in the
  UI and prefer HTTPS URLs when the user provides them.
- Never disable certificate validation or add trust-all managers.

## Permissions

- Camera is requested only when the user opens the QR scanner, with rationale and
  a manual fallback when denied.
- `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is requested only after explaining why: once, in the dialog shown
  after the first connection, or from the Settings switch. Declining turns notifications
  off. The `dataSync` foreground service runs only while sessions run, notifications are on
  and the permission is granted. Attention notifications are `VISIBILITY_PRIVATE` with a generic public version,
  and their Allow/Reject actions require an unlocked device.
- Do not add a permission without explicit need.

## Credentials And Sensitive Data

- Server passwords and pairing tokens live only in `ServerRepository`'s encrypted
  storage (`androidx.security:security-crypto` on Android, the Keychain on iOS via
  `KeychainServerStore`). Do not migrate it during
  unrelated work; a migration must define behavior for existing ciphertext,
  invalid keys and backup.
- `allowBackup` is false; keep secrets out of backups.
- Never log secrets, Authorization headers, pairing codes/links, prompts,
  transcripts, tool output or file contents. HTTP logging is debug-only with
  headers redacted and no bodies.
- Clipboard: read only on explicit user action ("Paste link"); never copy secrets.
  iOS asks the user before every programmatic paste.
- iOS mirrors the Android policy in `iosApp/iosApp/Info.plist`: ATS allows plain
  HTTP (self-hosted servers), and every permission has a usage description. Add a
  new iOS permission only with its description string (`kmp-ios`).
- Never put credentials in repository files, Maestro flows, screenshots,
  process-visible commands or final responses.

## Verification

Inspect the merged manifest after manifest changes and verify that malformed
links, wrong credentials and denied permissions fail closed without exposing
internal exception details.

name: android-testing
description: Use when adding or reviewing opencode-mobile unit tests (commonTest with kotlin.test or JVM androidHostTest), MVI ViewModel tests, repository fakes, recorded API fixtures, SSE/transcript tests, coroutine/Flow tests, Compose behavior tests, or test infrastructure.

# Android Testing

Use the narrowest deterministic test that proves the behavior. Unit and Compose
tests cover logic and UI contracts; Maestro covers a few complete journeys.

## Where Tests Live

- **`src/commonTest`** with `kotlin.test` and `kotlinx-coroutines-test` is the default
  for pure logic (reducers, mappers, parsers, formatting, ViewModels with fakes). It
  runs on the JVM with the host tests and on iOS with
  `./gradlew :<module>:iosSimulatorArm64Test` (Mac only). `core:domain` and `core:mvi`
  already test there; add `commonTest.dependencies { implementation(libs.kotlin.test) }`
  to a module the first time.
- **`src/androidHostTest`** (JVM, JUnit 4) for tests that need JVM tooling: OkHttp
  `MockWebServer` transport tests in `core:network`/`core:data` (the Android Ktor engine
  is OkHttp), Robolectric/Room, `MainDispatcherRule` from `core:testing`, classpath
  fixtures. Move such a test to `commonTest` only when it no longer needs them (e.g.
  with Ktor `MockEngine` and inline fixtures); migrate incrementally, never in bulk.
- Recorded, sanitized server fixtures (JSON responses and an `.sse` event log) live in
  `core/testing/src/main/resources` and are read from the JVM classpath.
- Compose UI test APIs for instrumented tests; Maestro for black-box Android flows;
  iOS runtime behavior is verified on the simulator (`kmp-ios`).

Do not add a new framework automatically (Turbine, Robolectric, screenshot
testing, mocking libraries) without a concrete requirement.

## What To Test

- Mapping of generated API models to domain models against fixtures.
- Event decoding and `TranscriptReducer` replay of recorded streams.
- `ConnectLinkParser`, error mapping, auth headers and pairing requests.
- ViewModels: State transitions and Effects with fake repositories.
- Do not unit-test Compose layout declarations, Activities or DI registration.

Prefer fakes over mocks. Use `runTest`, virtual time and `advanceUntilIdle`;
never `Thread.sleep` or real delays.

```text
initial State -> onEvent -> fake response or failure -> State transition -> Effect if transient
```

## Fixtures

- Record fixtures only from scratch sessions in a disposable directory, then
  replace paths with neutral ones (`/home/user/project`), strip reasoning signatures and system
  instructions, and never include secrets, private paths or personal prompts.
- When the server version changes, refresh fixtures and keep the old ones only
  if they cover a compatibility case.

## Flow And Effects

- Assert ordered emissions when sequence matters.
- Start collecting Effects before triggering the event.

## Compose Behavior Tests

- Test stateless screens from supplied State without the Koin graph.
- Every interactive control keeps a stable `testTag`; prefer semantic matchers.
- Cover loading, empty, error, content, streaming and disabled states.

## Verification

Run the focused module test first (`./gradlew :<module>:testDebugUnitTest`, an alias of
`testAndroidHostTest`, which also runs `commonTest` on the JVM), then `./gradlew
spotlessCheck testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug compileKotlinIosArm64
compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` from `android/`. See
`references/test-matrix.md` for risk-based evidence.

description: Use for the opencode-mobile iOS app — iosApp Xcode project, Info.plist and permissions, the Shared framework and MainViewController, Compose Multiplatform behavior on iOS (keyboard, insets, accessibility, lifecycle), Keychain and signing, ATS, Darwin Ktor engine, building on the Mac and runtime verification on the iOS simulator.

# iOS App

The iOS app is a thin SwiftUI host (`iosApp/iosApp/iOSApp.swift`) around the shared
Compose UI returned by `MainViewController()` in
`android/shared/src/iosMain`. Almost all behavior lives in Kotlin.

## Integration

- Direct integration: the Xcode build phase runs
  `./gradlew :shared:embedAndSignAppleFrameworkForXcode` from `android/` (needs
  `JAVA_HOME`). The framework is static, named `Shared`; nothing is exported to
  Swift. No CocoaPods, no SwiftPM, no XCFramework.
- Swift only hosts `ComposeView` with `.ignoresSafeArea()`; Compose handles insets.
  SKIE or Swift export are not used: add them only when Swift code must consume
  Kotlin `Flow` or `suspend` APIs.
- Targets: `iosArm64` (devices) and `iosSimulatorArm64` (Apple Silicon simulators).
  No `iosX64`.
- Koin starts once in `MainViewController()` with `dataModule` and `sharedModule`.
- `Info.plist` owns permission strings (camera, microphone, speech recognition,
  photo library, local network) and ATS: `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` because servers
  are self-hosted over plain HTTP on LAN/VPN, like Android's cleartext policy.
- Simulator builds are ad-hoc signed (`CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY[sdk=iphonesimulator*] =
  "-"`): an unsigned app cannot use the Keychain (`errSecMissingEntitlement`,
  -34018). Device builds need `TEAM_ID` in `iosApp/Configuration/Config.xcconfig`.
- `MARKETING_VERSION` lives in `Config.xcconfig` and is bumped by release-please with
  `version.txt`; do not set it in `project.pbxproj`.

## Compose On iOS

- Keyboard: `ComposeUIViewController(configure = { onFocusBehavior =
  OnFocusBehavior.DoNothing })` because screens use `imePadding()`; the default
  behavior shifts the focused field a second time.
- iOS has no Back key to close the keyboard: the app root clears focus on taps
  outside controls (`dismissKeyboardOnTap`, iOS actual only).
- Back navigation uses `OcBackHandler` (navigation-event back gesture on iOS).
- Lifecycle maps to Android states (background → `ON_STOP`); the event stream
  pauses in the background (`ApplicationStateVisibility`) and resumes on return.
- `testTag` does not become an accessibility identifier; UI automation and
  VoiceOver use labels. Every icon-only control needs a content description.
- Strings, fonts and plurals come from Compose resources and follow the app
  language (`AppleLanguages`); numbers and dates use `NSNumberFormatter` /
  `NSDateFormatter` / `NSRelativeDateTimeFormatter` actuals.

## Platform Services

| Concern | iOS implementation |
|---|---|
| Credentials | `KeychainServerStore` (multiplatform-settings `KeychainSettings`) |
| Settings, drafts | `NSUserDefaultsSettings` suites `settings`, `drafts` |
| Transcript cache | Room with `BundledSQLiteDriver`, file in Caches |
| Network changes | `NWPathMonitor` (`PathNetworkMonitor`) |
| LAN discovery | `getifaddrs` on `en*` interfaces |
| HTTP | Ktor Darwin engine; it ignores `connectTimeoutMillis`, only request and socket timeouts apply |
| Clipboard | `UIPasteboard` (iOS asks before the app pastes) |
| QR, dictation, picker | AVFoundation, Speech + AVAudioEngine, PHPicker / document picker |
| Terminal | xterm.js page from Compose resources in a `WKWebView` (`UIKitView`, non-cooperative touches); bridge over `WKScriptMessageHandler`, font injected as a user script |
| Links | `opencodemobile://session/<id>`, `opencodemobile://new-session` (`AppLinks.kt`, `.onOpenURL` in `iOSApp.swift`) |
| Home screen widget | WidgetKit extension `iosApp/SessionsWidget` (SwiftUI); the app writes a JSON snapshot to the App Group (`WidgetSnapshots.kt`) and calls `WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines` |
| Notifications | not supported; settings section hidden |

## Widget Extension

- The extension cannot reach the server or the Keychain: it only reads
  `widget.snapshot` from the App Group defaults (`OCAppGroup` in both Info.plists, from
  `APP_GROUP` in `Config.xcconfig`). Change the JSON contract in `WidgetSnapshots.kt` and
  `SessionsWidget.swift` together.
- The snapshot is written at launch and on `widgetRefreshes` (sessions start, end or are
  deleted, the server changes, the app goes to the background).
- Strings come from the Android widget strings: `bun tools/ios-widget-strings.ts`
  regenerates `Localizable.xcstrings`; `tools/ios-widget-strings.test.ts` fails when stale.
- Device builds need the App Group enabled for `TEAM_ID`; the simulator needs nothing.
- `iosApp.xcodeproj` is edited by hand (no generator): new files need a file reference, a
  group entry and a build phase entry in `project.pbxproj`.

## Build And Verify On The Mac

Linking needs macOS with Xcode; Linux only compiles klibs. Sync the worktree to
the Mac, then from `iosApp/`:

```bash
xcodebuild -project iosApp.xcodeproj -target iosApp -configuration Debug \
  -sdk iphonesimulator -arch arm64 SYMROOT=$HOME/ocm-build build
xcrun simctl install booted $HOME/ocm-build/Debug-iphonesimulator/OpenCodeMobile.app
xcrun simctl launch booted io.github.beppe2880.opencodemobile
```

- Only build the debug simulator framework while iterating; never
  `linkRelease*` or XCFrameworks locally. For slow builds load
  `kotlin-tooling-native-build-performance` (its audit takes `android` as the Gradle
  project root: `scripts/audit-native-build.sh android`).
- Shared tests run on the simulator with `./gradlew :<module>:iosSimulatorArm64Test`.
- Runtime checks: pair against a disposable OpenCode server on the Mac
  (`opencode pair --url http://localhost:<port>`), never the user's personal
  server; exercise the changed screen; read crashes in
  `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/OpenCodeMobile-*.ips` and logs with
  `xcrun simctl spawn booted log show --predicate 'process == "OpenCodeMobile"'`.
- Automation details (DeviceKit JSON-RPC, coordinates, screenshots) are in
  `references/simulator-automation.md`.
- Never show pairing codes or passwords in screenshots or reports.

# KMP Master

Use this as the router for work in `android/` (all Kotlin Multiplatform modules) and
`iosApp/`. Read `android/AGENTS.md`, the files being changed, and one comparable
implementation before editing.

## Route To The Smallest Skill Set

- Load `android-compose-mvi` for Compose screens, state ownership, effects,
  route/screen boundaries, the `Oc*` design system, insets, or IME.
- Load `android-navigation` for the connect/main graph, type-safe routes, route
  arguments, back handling, or list-detail layouts.
- Load `android-auth-session` for pairing, server passwords, saved servers,
  credential storage, 401 handling, or active-server switching.
- Load `android-opencode-api` for the generated client in `core/api`, the Ktor
  client, SSE events, mapping to domain models, or regenerating the API.
- Load `android-data-boundaries` for repository contracts, local stores,
  domain mapping, transcript reconciliation, or typed data errors.
- Load `android-coroutines` for scopes, suspend APIs, Flow, the shared event
  stream, cancellation, dispatchers, or reconnection.
- Load `android-koin` for dependency registration and runtime parameters.
- Load `kmp-platform-boundaries` whenever code needs a platform API, a new
  `expect`/`actual`, or a decision between `commonMain`, `androidMain` and `iosMain`.
- Load `kmp-ios` for `iosApp/`, Info.plist, the Shared framework, iOS-specific
  Compose behavior, Keychain/ATS/Darwin, and building or verifying on the Mac.
- Load `kotlin-tooling-native-build-performance` only for slow iOS/native builds.
- Load `android-gradle` for modules, Kotlin Multiplatform targets, dependencies,
  the version catalog, SDK/AGP configuration, or build types.
- Load `android-testing` for non-trivial logic changes, regression fixes,
  fixtures, fakes, dispatcher control, or test infrastructure.
- Load `android-localization-accessibility` for user-visible copy (English and
  Italian), semantics, TalkBack, focus, RTL, font scale, or adaptive layout.
- Load `android-security` for manifests, cleartext policy, camera permission,
  credential storage, clipboard, or sensitive logging.
- Load `android-performance` only for an evidenced startup, streaming jank,
  recomposition, APK size, R8, memory, or trace problem.
- Load `android-benchmarks` to measure performance or add a performance test: the
  `android/benchmark` Macrobenchmark module, idle frames and CPU, cold start, scroll.
- Load `maestro` only for `.maestro/` test flows.
- Load `android-runtime-verification` after Android behavior/UI changes and for
  install, emulator, ADB, Logcat, crash, or runtime-debug work; shared UI or
  iOS-specific changes are also verified on the iOS simulator (`kmp-ios`).

Do not load adjacent skills speculatively. A chat screen change may need
`android-compose-mvi` and `android-data-boundaries`; a color change does not.

## Cross-Skill Boundaries

- Credential storage changes use `android-auth-session` plus `android-security`;
  HTTP client changes also use `android-opencode-api`.
- Live event handling uses `android-opencode-api` (decoding),
  `android-data-boundaries` (transcript reduction) and `android-coroutines`
  (stream ownership).
- Koin owns binding and lifetime; Gradle owns which module compiles it.
- Performance work requires evidence. Compose does not optimize speculatively.

## Project Invariants

- Code is shared by default: `commonMain` holds domain, data, UI and ViewModels;
  platform code stays in `androidMain`/`iosMain` (`kmp-platform-boundaries`).
- Dependency direction is `app -> shared -> feature -> core`. Features depend on
  `core:domain`, `core:ui`, `core:mvi` and the repository interfaces; they never
  depend on `:app`, `core:network` or `core:api`.
- `core:api` is generated by `tools/api-gen` (`bun run generate`). Never edit it and never
  hand-write DTOs for OpenCode payloads.
- Generated API models stay inside `core:network`/`core:data`; the UI consumes
  domain models from `core:domain`.
- Screen composables receive immutable state and callbacks. Thin route
  composables resolve ViewModels, collect state/effects and bridge navigation.
- ViewModels extend `BaseViewModel<State, Event, Effect>` from `core:mvi`.
- Use `Oc*` components and `OcTheme`/`MaterialTheme` tokens from `core:ui`.
- Every interactive control has a stable `testTag`.

## Modern But Boring

Prefer the simplest modern solution that fits the existing architecture. Do not
introduce a UseCase, Manager, Coordinator, extra mapper layer, custom Flow
wrapper, custom scope, or Gradle convention plugin unless the problem benefits
from it or an established project pattern requires it.

Do not perform opportunistic migrations: no Navigation 3, Room 3, Koin annotations,
SKIE, Swift export, a new DI framework, or a new storage framework during unrelated
work. Room KMP (with KSP) is used only for the transcript and session-list caches in
`core/data/cache`; settings and credentials keep their existing stores (SharedPreferences
and EncryptedSharedPreferences on Android, NSUserDefaults and Keychain on iOS).

## Completion

Run module-qualified checks from `android/`, then `./gradlew spotlessCheck
testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug compileKotlinIosArm64
compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` for broad changes. Load `android-runtime-verification`
when runtime behavior can change. Report checks run, device used, and anything
that could not be verified.

description: Use when opencode-mobile Kotlin Multiplatform code under android/ needs platform-specific behavior or placement decisions — commonMain vs androidMain vs iosMain, expect/actual vs interfaces bound in Koin, java.*/android.* APIs leaking into common code, platform replacements (kotlinx-datetime, kotlin.time.Clock, Uuid, atomicfu, Base64), BuildConfig-like values, or new platform features.
